title: Explainability
html:
Explainability answers why a model predicts what it does — globally (which features drive the model) and locally (why this one prediction). It builds trust, finds bugs and leakage, and is required in regulated decisions.

MethodScopeIdeaCaveats
Interpretable model (linear, small tree)Global + localThe model is the explanationCoefficients need comparable scales; correlated features muddle them
Impurity importance (MDI)GlobalTotal impurity decrease from a feature's splitsTraining-data based; biased toward continuous/high-cardinality features
Permutation importanceGlobalScore drop when a feature's values are shuffledCorrelated features share/hide importance; shuffling creates unrealistic rows
Partial dependence (PDP) / ICEGlobal / per rowAverage prediction as one feature variesAverages can hide interactions; assumes feature independence
SHAPLocal (aggregates to global)Shapley-value attribution of each feature's contributionCostly for general models; depends on the background data; not causal
LIMELocalFit a simple surrogate model on perturbed samples around one rowUnstable across runs; depends on the perturbation scheme
CounterfactualsLocalSmallest input change that flips the decisionMay suggest changes that aren't actionable

Permutation vs impurity importance

Five generated features (0–2 informative, 3–4 pure noise), plus a random continuous column (5) and a random 3-level category (6). Labels are noisy, so the forest's deep trees happily split on noise:

Impurity importance hands the continuous noise column almost half the credit of a real feature — and much more than the equally useless 3-level category, because a feature with many distinct values offers many candidate splits. Permutation importance on held-out data correctly gives all noise columns about zero.

Partial dependence

SHAP in one idea

SHAP treats features as players in a cooperative game whose payout is the prediction. A feature's Shapley value is its average marginal contribution over all orders in which features could be added. Key property (efficiency): the contributions add up exactly to prediction − baseline (the average prediction). Other properties: symmetric features get equal credit; a feature that never changes the output gets 0.

f(x) = φ₀ + Σⱼ φⱼ φ₀ = E[f(X)] linear model, independent features: φⱼ = wⱼ · (xⱼ − E[xⱼ])

The shap package computes these for any model — exactly and quickly for tree ensembles (TreeSHAP), approximately for others (KernelSHAP) — and draws summary, dependence and waterfall plots.

Watch out

Explanations describe the model, not the world: a large SHAP value means the model relies on the feature, not that changing the feature would change the outcome. With correlated features, credit is split in ways that depend on the method.

What is the difference between interpretability and explainability?

Interpretability usually means the model is understandable by design (linear model, small tree). Explainability means post-hoc techniques (permutation importance, PDP, SHAP, LIME, counterfactuals) that explain a model that may be a black box.

Why prefer permutation importance over a random forest's feature_importances_?

Impurity-based importance is computed on training data and inflates features with many possible split points (continuous or high-cardinality), even pure noise. Permutation importance measures the actual drop in a held-out score when a feature is scrambled, so irrelevant features score about zero.

How does SHAP work?

It assigns each feature its Shapley value — the average change in the prediction when that feature is added, over all possible orders of adding features, relative to a background expectation. The values are additive (they sum to prediction minus the baseline), consistent and fair in the game-theoretic sense; TreeSHAP computes them exactly for tree models.
